R2.passage: Dear Ricardo, Welcome to our house, and thank you for staying and watching our dog while we are away. The bathroom is next to the bedroom, so you will find it easily. You can use anything in there. The soap is in the shower. There is a towel on the counter, near the sink, and another one under it. There is an extra toothbrush under the sink in a blue packet, and there is also a comb under the toilet, which is not the best place for a comb but it is where it always ends up. Make yourself at home! Thanks, Clare

R4.passage: Some ant colonies are in trees, but most ant colonies are under the ground. Ants dig in the dirt and bring it up, and the pile they make becomes an ant hill. Inside, an ant colony has different rooms: a room for food, a room for raising young ants, and a room for the queen. Sometimes an ant colony is bigger than a person. Some people keep pet ants in a glass case filled with sand, and they call it an ant farm because you can look inside and watch the ants at work. Left alone, the colony keeps building: the rooms get deeper, the pile outside gets taller, and nothing in it belongs to one ant.

phonics.note: Optional pronunciation card inside the Speaking station. The book contrasts r and l here.
phonics.note2: The trap is that r and l are the hardest contrast for many learners, and both appear in this unit's own vocabulary: rope (r), towel (l), porch (r), ball (l). Say the pairs slowly before any recording.

speechScoring.reuse: Same engine as Units 1-4: browser Web Speech API, keyword coverage, bands only, never a numeric grade.
additions: Contractions are central: accept it's / it is, they're / they are, isn't / is not, aren't / are not.
Accept 'toothbrush' variants and 'swing set' / 'swingset' as the same keyword.
Plural endings carry the grammar here: if the learner says 'where is' for 'where are', show the form rather than failing the item at Easy and Core.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some rooms and things in a house.
vocabulary.core: I can name objects and the places in a house and garden.
vocabulary.challenging: I can talk about where things belong and why.

grammar.easy: I can say where one thing is.
grammar.core: I can use Where is and Where are, and It's and They're.
grammar.challenging: I can keep the question, the short answer and the full answer the same number.

listening.easy: I can hear an object word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand where something is.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description and catch a negative.

reading.easy: I can read a short note about where things are.
reading.core: I can find where things are in a note.
reading.challenging: I can understand a joke or an aside in a note.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence with in, on or under.
writing.core: I can fill a chart showing where things are.
writing.challenging: I can describe a room and give reasons.

speaking.easy: I can tell someone where my things are.
speaking.core: I can ask and answer Where is and Where are.
speaking.challenging: I can describe a room for a minute.
